text:
ashley: heads up — main CI turned red right after the merge from @ben. The smoke job is hanging on the step 'write-lockfile' for ~10m, no progress logs :exclamation:
ci-bot: [CI] Pipeline: main #4827 — FAIL
ci-bot: failed step: write-lockfile (timeout)
ci-bot: logs: https://ci.internal/redact/4827/logs
ben: oof, that was my dep update PR. I only changed a small pipfile. I can look but may be on a call for 20m, ping me if it looks like a config drift
maria: @ashley any rerun yet? can we quick-rerun the job to see if it's a flake? :eyes:
ashley: not yet — logs show repeated EAGAIN on open() when trying to write /workspace/.lock
ashley: snippet:
```
[2025-05-14T18:12:03Z] ERROR write-lockfile: open /workspace/.lock: resource temporarily unavailable
[2025-05-14T18:12:03Z] WARN retrying (1/5)
[2025-05-14T18:12:33Z] ERROR write-lockfile: open /workspace/.lock: resource temporarily unavailable
```
ben: hmm looks like a mount contention. Did we change the runner image or the workspace mounting in the pipeline? my change only touched pipfile but CI config unchanged
derek: I pushed a quick job to ssh into a failed node to inspect but we don't have direct access in the hosted runners. If it's a k8s ephemeral runner could be a kernel hang on overlayfs
oncall: I'm oncall — I can trigger a rerun and grab the raw node logs (if self-hosted). Rerun now?
maria: yes please rerun once, if it still fails we should bisect. Also add the artifact with full /var/log/syslog and containerd logs
oncall: rerun kicked off (pipeline #4828). tagging @ben and @derek for owner eyes.
ci-bot: [CI] Pipeline: main #4828 — RUNNING
ci-bot: step write-lockfile started
ci-bot: [CI] Pipeline: main #4828 — FAIL
ci-bot: failed step: write-lockfile (timeout)
ci-bot: logs: https://ci.internal/redact/4828/logs
ashley: same symptom. now it's deterministic on this runner pool. suspect an overlayfs/kernel regression or a stale process holding the lock
ben: could be the new pip package changed pip cache behavior? unlikely to lock /workspace but possible if install scripts run in entrypoint. I'll revert my pip change to be safe if we confirm it's the culprit
derek: quick check — can someone search recent infra deploys? I don't see infra merges in last 2 hours. @infra-deploy-bot?
ashley: infra-deploy-bot shows no infra rollouts in the timeframe
maria: plan: (1) isolate by running the job on a different runner pool (2) if fails on all pools, trigger a bisect on last 5 merges to main (3) if only on one pool, escalate to eng-infra to drain and repro on a repro node
oncall: draining pool now and rescheduling one run to pool-b. Kicking that rerun (#4829)
ci-bot: [CI] Pipeline: main #4829 — RUNNING
ci-bot: [CI] Pipeline: main #4829 — PASS
maria: ok green on pool-b — so it's localized to pool-a runners. tagging eng-infra to evict unhealthy instances and repro
derek: I'll take it. I'm going to rotate the pool and run the write-lockfile step interactively on a repro instance. If it's overlayfs we may need a kernel upgrade revert or node reprovision.
ben: thanks. if you want me to revert my PR while you probe, say the word and I'll open a revert PR.
ashley: not necessary yet — thanks everyone. @derek please post a short postmortem if you find root cause. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
